messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGED — GPU ECC threshold breach on cluster-gpu-prod-7. Severity: P2. Paging oncall team. Node: gpu-prod-7a (zone-us-west2). Symptoms: repeated Xid errors, container crashes, elevated 5xx for /v1/generate. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/serving/gpu-errors
Alex W: taking this — oncall here. quick status: any customer-facing errors confirmed?
Priya N: seeing repeated `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31` in dmesg on gpu-prod-7a. nvml shows ECC corrected count spiking. pods on that node show `OOMKilled` and `SIGABRT` in serving-runtime containers.
Sam R: looks like the ECC corrected errors keep leading to driver resets. I can cordon+drain node if we want to move traffic off.
Alex W: do it. route traffic to pool-gpu-hot in us-west2-b as fallback. Priya, can you paste the failing log tail?
Priya N: tail from kubelet/journalctl: ```
Mar 15 12:02:41 gpu-prod-7a kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=27435
Mar 15 12:02:41 gpu-prod-7a nvidia-smi: failed to query device: Unknown Error
Mar 15 12:02:42 gpu-prod-7a dockerd: container abc123 exited with code 137
```
Jin L: Confirmed increased 5xx on hosted-api-prod: 4xx->5xx ratio up 6% in last 3m. Two mid-tier customers report degraded latency. Not yet full outage but user requests are erroring.
oncall-sre: ack. Sam, proceed with cordon/drain. Prioritize canary pods first.
Sam R: running commands now: ```
kubectl cordon gpu-prod-7a
kubectl drain gpu-prod-7a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```
Sam R: drain in progress — some stateful pods stuck (checkpointing). I'll force evict long-running tasks after 90s.
Alex W: ops note — do NOT reboot node yet. We want to collect nvram/dmesg dumps and nvml logs for infra. Priya, capture `nvidia-smi -q` and `dmesg -T | tail -n 200`.
Priya N: uploaded logs to /shared/incidents/2024500000/logs.tar.gz and attached to ticket INC-2024-1587. nvml shows ECC corrected errors on GPU 0 and 1, memory-err increase: +120 in last 10m.
Jin L: customer-impact summary for slack thread: two customers (~0.8% of requests) saw errors; internal alerting fired for SLO breach. No data exfiltration.
Alex W: mitigation steps so far: 1) cordon+drain node 2) route traffic to fallback pool 3) collect logs 4) escalate to hw/infra for hardware check. Next: decide reboot vs. isolate GPU.
Priya N: quick check: driver version is 525.125; kernel 6.2.7. There are known driver releases with stability fixes for our card gen. If we reboot container runtime it sometimes recovers but flips again.
Sam R: drain complete. All pods rescheduled. Traffic rerouted. 5xx rate dropping toward baseline.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: AUTO-RUN: scaled up pool-gpu-hot by +2 nodes per autoscaler policy.
Alex W: Agree we should repro with one workload on a spare node before full reboot. Jin, spin up a staging run with same model and load for 15m to try to reproduce Xid.
Jin L: started repro job (staging-gpu-repro-42). Observing similar Xid 31 after ~7m under heavy seqlen-2048 load.
Priya N: given repro, likelihood is hardware instability or a driver/kernel interaction under long KV cache usage. Recommend swap out GPU or schedule maintenance to update driver after-hours.
Sam R: I'm going to request a node reboot and a hardware diagnostic from infra. Steps: `ssh gpu-prod-7a && sudo systemctl stop kubelet docker && sudo reboot`. Will wait for infra signoff.
oncall-sre: infra ticket created: INFRA-6742. Hardware team assigned. ETA initial triage 30m.
Alex W: assign postmortem owner — Priya? can you take lead? we'll compile timeline and customer impact.
Priya N: I can. I'll draft initial timeline and assign action items: follow-up driver upgrade, add extra nvml telemetry (per-GPU corrected/uncorrected counters), expand fallback capacity, and run a long-run stress test.
Sam R: post-incident short term remediation: quarantined node (cordoned), scheduled reboot & hw diag, increased routing capacity. Long term: test driver/kernel matrix, automated automated GPU health-based node fencing.
Alex W: communication: notify affected customers with a short incident update: "We experienced transient GPU driver resets causing increased errors for some requests; we've isolated the node and rerouted traffic; ongoing diagnostics." Jin, can you draft?
Jin L: drafting now. I'll post to #customer-impact and PMs.
incident-bot: :hourglass_flowing_sand: HANDOFF — oncall shift ending in 20m. Alex, please confirm handoff state.
Alex W: Handoff OK. State: node cordoned+drained, logs collected, hw diag ticket open, staging repro confirmed Xid 31 under load, customer impact limited but visible. Priya will own postmortem. Sam will follow infra tasks.
Priya N: adding checklist to incident ticket: timeline, logs link, repro artifacts, postmortem owner, follow-up tech tasks.
Sam R: leaving note — if driver upgrade scheduled, plan a staged canary across pool-gpu-hot then full rollout. Use canary fraction 5% then 25% then 100%.
Jin L: customers notified. No escalation to P1.
Alex W: closing active paging for now — monitoring for 1h. If recurs, we'll escalate to P1. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
